\section{Introduction}

\subsection{The motivating question and its category error}

The starting point of this work was the request to construct \emph{a surface of Hausdorff dimension $\aleph_1$}, and to prove that such a surface embeds in the Hilbert cube but in no finite-dimensional Euclidean space.

Taken literally the request is not satisfiable, and the reason is structural rather than technical. Hausdorff dimension is a function
\[
\dimH : \{\text{subsets of a metric space}\} \longrightarrow [0,\infty],
\]
whose codomain is a linearly ordered set of cardinality $\cc$ but of \emph{order type} that of the extended real line. Cardinal numbers such as $\aleph_1$ are not among its values. The natural repair --- to produce a transfinite hierarchy of sets whose dimensions increase strictly along $\omega_1$ and to call the limit ``the $\aleph_1$-st dimension'' --- also fails, and we prove that it fails necessarily (Theorem~\ref{thm:ceiling2}): every well-ordered chain of Hausdorff dimensions is countable.

What \emph{does} exist, and what this paper constructs, is the object the phrase was reaching for: a bounded set with $\dimH = \infty$ built entirely out of ordinary finite-dimensional boxes; with exactly $\aleph_1$ points under the Continuum Hypothesis; embedding topologically in the Hilbert cube; and admitting no bounded-distortion image in any $\R^m$ and no triangulation whatsoever.

\subsection{The two categories}

The question ``does this surface fit in $\R^m$?'' has different answers in the topological and metric categories. In the topological category, non-embeddability is a statement of covering-dimension theory. In the metric category, non-embeddability follows immediately from Hausdorff dimension monotonicity, and it is strictly sharper than anything cardinality can give: the surface has exactly $\cc$ points, the same as $\R^m$, so counting is blind here. We therefore prove the metric statement in its strongest form (Theorem~\ref{thm:noanti}): there is not even an \emph{antilipschitz} map, that is, no map $f$ with $\|f(x)-f(y)\| \ge K^{-1} d(x,y)$, into a finite-dimensional normed space. Every bi-Lipschitz embedding is in particular antilipschitz.

\section{The ambient space and the coordinate maps}

Throughout, $\ell^2 = \ell^2(\N;\R)$ is the real Hilbert space of square-summable sequences with norm $\|x\| = (\sum_i x_i^2)^{1/2}$, and $\dimH A \in [0,\infty]$ is the Hausdorff dimension of $A$. We use two standard facts and essentially nothing else.

\begin{fact}[Lipschitz monotonicity]\label{fact:A}
If $f : A \to Y$ satisfies $d(f(x),f(y)) \le K\,d(x,y)$ on $A$, then $\dimH f(A) \le \dimH A$.
\end{fact}

\begin{fact}[Countable stability]\label{fact:B}
For any countable family $\{A_j\}$, $\dimH \bigcup_j A_j = \sup_j \dimH A_j$.
\end{fact}

Fact~\ref{fact:A} applied twice in opposite directions is the engine of every dimension computation below; Fact~\ref{fact:A} alone, applied to three different diagrams, is the engine of every impossibility theorem.

\begin{definition}[Box sides]
For $i \in \N$ set $\sigma_i = 2^{-i}$. Then $0 < \sigma_i \le 1$ and $\sum_i \sigma_i^2 = \sum_i 4^{-i} = \tfrac43$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Extension by zero]
For $n \in \N$ define $\iota_n : \R^n \to \ell^2$ by $(\iota_n y)_i = y_i$ for $i<n$ and $(\iota_n y)_i = 0$ for $i \ge n$, where $\R^n$ carries the \emph{sup norm} $\|y\|_\infty = \max_{i<n}|y_i|$. The image is finitely supported, hence square-summable, so $\iota_n$ is a well-defined injective linear map.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate projection]
For $n \in \N$ define $\pi_n : \ell^2 \to (\R^n,\|\cdot\|_\infty)$ by $\pi_n(x) = (x_0,\dots,x_{n-1})$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:section}
$\pi_n \circ \iota_n = \mathrm{id}_{\R^n}$; in particular $\iota_n$ is injective.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Projection is $1$-Lipschitz]\label{lem:pi}
$\|\pi_n x - \pi_n x'\|_\infty \le \|x-x'\|$ for all $x,x' \in \ell^2$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Each coordinate functional obeys $|z_i| \le \|z\|$ for $z \in \ell^2$; apply this to $z = x-x'$ and maximise over $i<n$.
\end{proof}

The same argument shows each coordinate functional $x \mapsto x_i$ is $1$-Lipschitz, hence continuous.

\begin{lemma}[Extension is $\sqrt n$-Lipschitz]\label{lem:iota}
$\|\iota_n y\| \le \sqrt n\,\|y\|_\infty$; since $\iota_n$ is linear, $\iota_n$ is $\sqrt n$-Lipschitz.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At most $n$ coordinates of $\iota_n y$ are nonzero, each of modulus at most $\|y\|_\infty$, so $\|\iota_n y\|^2 = \sum_{i<n} y_i^2 \le n\|y\|_\infty^2$.
\end{proof}

The pair $(\pi_n,\iota_n)$ is a Lipschitz section--retraction pair: $\iota_n$ embeds $\R^n$ with distortion at most $\sqrt n$, and $\pi_n$ undoes it with no distortion at all. That two-sided control is what pins Hausdorff dimension.

\section{Cells, the surface, and their dimensions}

\begin{definition}
$B_n = \prod_{i<n}[0,\sigma_i] \subseteq (\R^n,\|\cdot\|_\infty)$.
\end{definition}

$B_n$ is compact, nonempty, and has nonempty interior since every $\sigma_i>0$; hence $\dimH B_n = n$.

\begin{definition}[Cells and the surface]
The \emph{$n$-th cell} is $C_n = \iota_n(B_n) \subseteq \ell^2$, and the \emph{aleph-one surface} is
\[
\surf = \bigcup_{n\in\N} C_n .
\]
\end{definition}

Concretely $C_n = \{x \in \ell^2 : 0 \le x_i \le 2^{-i} \text{ for } i<n,\ x_i=0 \text{ for } i \ge n\}$, a flat compact $n$-dimensional box in the span of the first $n$ coordinate axes.

\begin{lemma}[Nesting]
$C_n \subseteq C_{n+1}$; hence $\surf$ is an increasing union.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Exact cell dimension]\label{thm:cell}
$\dimH C_n = n$ for every $n \in \N$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Upper bound: $C_n = \iota_n(B_n)$ with $\iota_n$ Lipschitz (Lemma~\ref{lem:iota}), so $\dimH C_n \le \dimH B_n = n$ by Fact~\ref{fact:A}. Lower bound: $\pi_n(C_n) = B_n$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:section}, and $\pi_n$ is $1$-Lipschitz (Lemma~\ref{lem:pi}), so $n = \dimH B_n = \dimH \pi_n(C_n) \le \dimH C_n$.
\end{proof}

The two Lipschitz constants never enter the conclusion; only their finiteness matters. Hausdorff dimension is insensitive to bounded distortion --- precisely why it is the right invariant for the impossibility theorems and the wrong one for topological questions.

\begin{theorem}[Transfinite dimension]\label{thm:top}
$\dimH \surf = \infty$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
By Fact~\ref{fact:B}, $\dimH \surf = \sup_n \dimH C_n = \sup_n n = \infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
For every real $d \ge 0$ the $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of $\surf$ is infinite. In particular $\surf$ has infinite length, area, volume and $d$-measure at every fractional $d$.
\end{corollary}

\section{Transfinite-dimensional sets and three obstructions}

\begin{definition}
A subset $A$ of a metric space is \emph{transfinite-dimensional} if $\dimH A = \infty$.
\end{definition}

Transfinite-dimensionality is inherited by supersets, and since countable sets have dimension $0$, every transfinite-dimensional set is uncountable. By Theorem~\ref{thm:top}, $\surf$ is transfinite-dimensional.

\begin{theorem}[No bounded-distortion picture in finite dimensions]\label{thm:noanti}
Let $A$ be transfinite-dimensional and let $F$ be a finite-dimensional normed space. Then there is no $K<\infty$ and map $f : A \to F$ with $\|f(x)-f(y)\| \ge K^{-1} d(x,y)$ for all $x,y \in A$. In particular $A$ admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into any $\R^m$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
An antilipschitz map cannot decrease dimension: its inverse on the image is $K$-Lipschitz, so $\dimH A \le \dimH f(A)$ by Fact~\ref{fact:A}. But $f(A) \subseteq F$ and every subset of a finite-dimensional normed space has dimension at most $\dim F$. Hence $\infty \le \dim F < \infty$, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Lipschitz $d$-triangulation]\label{def:tri}
A \emph{Lipschitz $d$-triangulation} of $A \subseteq X$ consists of a \emph{countable} index set $J$, parameter domains $D_j \subseteq \R^d$, and maps $\varphi_j : \R^d \to X$ with constants $K_j<\infty$ such that $\varphi_j$ is $K_j$-Lipschitz on $D_j$, subject only to $A \subseteq \bigcup_{j \in J}\varphi_j(D_j)$.
\end{definition}

No injectivity, disjointness, simpliciality, closedness or local finiteness is required; cells may be curved, overlapping, and countably infinite in number. Any classical simplicial or CW triangulation by $d$-simplices is a Lipschitz $d$-triangulation.

\begin{lemma}\label{lem:tri}
If $A$ admits a Lipschitz $d$-triangulation then $\dimH A \le d$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
$\dimH A \le \dimH \bigcup_j \varphi_j(D_j) = \sup_j \dimH \varphi_j(D_j) \le \sup_j \dimH D_j \le \dimH \R^d = d$, using Fact~\ref{fact:B} then Fact~\ref{fact:A}.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[No triangulation]\label{thm:notri}
A transfinite-dimensional set admits no Lipschitz $d$-triangulation for any $d \in \N$. In particular $\surf$ has no finite triangulation, and no countable one.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[No countable finite-dimensional $C^1$ atlas]
Let $A$ be a transfinite-dimensional subset of a normed space $F$, let $E$ be a finite-dimensional normed space, $J$ countable, $U_j \subseteq E$ convex, and $\varphi_j : E \to F$ of class $C^1$ on $U_j$. Then $A \not\subseteq \bigcup_{j\in J}\varphi_j(U_j)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A $C^1$ map on a convex set is Lipschitz there by the mean-value inequality, so as in Lemma~\ref{lem:tri} the cover would give $\dimH A \le \dim E < \infty$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Non-vacuity]
These are genuine obstructions. Section~\ref{sec:arith} constructs explicit Lipschitz $d$-triangulations of the truncated surfaces $\surf_S$ for every finite $S$, with exactly $|S|$ cells, and Section~\ref{sec:manifold} exhibits a transfinite-dimensional manifold.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[Why all three are one theorem]
Each impossibility result is the inequality $\dimH(\text{Lipschitz image}) \le \dimH(\text{source})$ read around a different diagram: for Theorem~\ref{thm:noanti} the Lipschitz map runs from $f(A)$ back to $A$; for the other two it runs from a finite-dimensional model into $X$.
\end{remark}

\section{Cardinality}

\begin{theorem}
$\#\surf = \cc$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
An element of $\ell^2$ is a function $\N \to \R$, and $\cc^{\aleph_0} = \cc$, so $\#\surf \le \#\ell^2 \le \cc$. Conversely $C_1 = \{(t,0,0,\dots) : t \in [0,1]\}$ is in bijection with $[0,1]$. Apply Cantor--Schr\"oder--Bernstein.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:CH}
Under the Continuum Hypothesis, $\#\surf = \aleph_1$.
\end{corollary}

The Continuum Hypothesis appears here and nowhere else, always as an explicit hypothesis. Corollary~\ref{cor:CH} is the only defensible sense in which the surface is an ``aleph-one surface'': $\aleph_1$ counts its points, never its dimension.

\section{The Hilbert box is a Hilbert cube}

Let $\Hbox = \{x \in \ell^2 : 0 \le x_i \le \sigma_i \text{ for all } i\}$ and $Q = [0,1]^{\N}$ with the product topology. Since each cell satisfies $0 \le x_i \le \sigma_i$ pointwise, $\surf \subseteq \Hbox$. The subtlety is that $\Hbox$ carries the $\ell^2$ metric topology while $Q$ carries the product topology; they agree on the box, but only because of a uniform tail estimate.

Let $\widetilde B = \prod_i [0,\sigma_i] \subseteq \R^{\N}$ with the product topology and $\Phi : \widetilde B \to \ell^2$ the tautological map $\Phi(y) = y$.

\begin{lemma}
Every $y \in \widetilde B$ is square-summable with $\|y\|^2 \le \sum_i 4^{-i} = \tfrac43$, so $\|\Phi(y)\| \le \sqrt{4/3} \approx 1.1547$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform tail estimate]\label{lem:tail}
Let $\Phi_N(y) = \iota_N(y_0,\dots,y_{N-1})$. Then for all $y \in \widetilde B$,
\[
\|\Phi(y)-\Phi_N(y)\|^2 = \sum_{i\ge N} y_i^2 \le \sum_{i\ge N} 4^{-i} = \tfrac43\,4^{-N} \le 2\cdot 2^{-N},
\]
a bound independent of $y$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}
$\Phi$ is continuous from the product topology to the $\ell^2$ norm topology.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Each $\Phi_N$ depends on finitely many coordinates and is product-continuous. By Lemma~\ref{lem:tail}, $\Phi_N \to \Phi$ uniformly with error $\le \sqrt{2\cdot 2^{-N}} \to 0$ geometrically at ratio $1/\sqrt2$. A uniform limit of continuous maps into a metric space is continuous.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:compact}
$\Phi$ is injective with image exactly $\Hbox$; hence $\Hbox$ is compact and $\Phi : \widetilde B \to \Hbox$ is a homeomorphism.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Injectivity and surjectivity onto $\Hbox$ are coordinatewise checks. By Tychonoff $\widetilde B$ is compact, so $\Hbox = \Phi(\widetilde B)$ is compact, and a continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space is a homeomorphism.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Hilbert box $\cong$ Hilbert cube]\label{thm:cube}
$\Hbox$ is homeomorphic to $Q = [0,1]^{\N}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\widetilde B$ is the product of the factors $[0,\sigma_i]$, each homeomorphic to $[0,1]$ by $t \mapsto t/\sigma_i$. Compose with Theorem~\ref{thm:compact}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Embedding theorem]\label{cor:embed}
Every subset of $\Hbox$ --- in particular $\surf$ and every arithmetic surface $\surf_S$ --- embeds topologically into the Hilbert cube $Q$ via $x \mapsto (x_i/\sigma_i)_i$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}
The surface embeds topologically in a compact space yet admits no bounded-distortion image in any $\R^m$. Both hold because \emph{Hausdorff dimension is not a topological invariant}: the homeomorphism of Theorem~\ref{thm:cube} multiplies distances in coordinate $i$ by $2^{i}$, and this unbounded distortion is exactly what lets a metrically transfinite object be topologically tame.
\end{remark}

\section{The surface as a dense skeleton; category versus dimension}

Let $\delta = (1,\tfrac12,\tfrac14,\dots) \in \Hbox$, the \emph{diagonal point}. Every point of $\surf$ has all but finitely many coordinates zero, so $\delta \notin \surf$; yet
\[
\operatorname{dist}(\delta, C_n) = \Big(\sum_{i\ge n} 4^{-i}\Big)^{1/2} = \frac{2}{\sqrt3}\,2^{-n} \longrightarrow 0 .
\]

\begin{theorem}[Closure]\label{thm:closure}
$\overline{\surf} = \Hbox$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\surf \subseteq \Hbox$ and $\Hbox$ is compact, hence closed, so $\overline{\surf}\subseteq \Hbox$. Conversely for $x \in \Hbox$ the truncations $\Phi_n(x) \in C_n \subseteq \surf$ satisfy $\|x-\Phi_n(x)\| \le \sqrt{\tfrac43 4^{-n}} \to 0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
$\surf$ is a dense proper subset of the compact set $\Hbox$, is $\sigma$-compact, and is neither closed nor compact. It is $\sigma$-finite-dimensional: a countable union of finite-dimensional sets whose total dimension is infinite.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Riesz, interior form]\label{thm:riesz}
In an infinite-dimensional real normed space every compact set has empty interior; hence compact sets are nowhere dense and $\sigma$-compact sets are meagre.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Ambient rigidity]
A normed space containing a transfinite-dimensional subset is infinite-dimensional and not locally compact.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The surface is meagre]
$\surf$ is nowhere dense and meagre in $\ell^2$, has empty interior, is not open, and its complement is dense.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
$\overline{\surf} = \Hbox$ is compact and $\ell^2$ is infinite-dimensional, so $\operatorname{int}\Hbox = \emptyset$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:riesz}; hence $\surf$ is nowhere dense, therefore meagre, with dense complement.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
$\ell^2$ is not $\sigma$-compact.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Otherwise $\ell^2$ would be meagre in itself, contradicting Baire's theorem for a complete space.
\end{proof}

So $\sigma$-compactness separates the surface from its ambient space: the surface, though dimension-theoretically maximal, is topologically thin and can never exhaust $\ell^2$.

\begin{theorem}[Every ball is transfinite-dimensional]\label{thm:ball}
For every $x \in \ell^2$ and $r>0$, $\dimH B(x,r) = \infty$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Fix $n$ and set $s = r/(2(\sqrt n +1))>0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:iota} the flat cube $\iota_n([0,s]^n)$ has norm at most $\sqrt n\,s \le r/2$, so its translate by $x$ lies in $B(x,r)$. Translation is an isometry, and the squeeze of Theorem~\ref{thm:cell} applies verbatim to a cube of side $s$, giving dimension $n$. Hence $n \le \dimH B(x,r)$ for all $n$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}
Any subset of $\ell^2$ with nonempty interior is transfinite-dimensional.
\end{corollary}

\begin{theorem}[Dimension--category dichotomy]
Let $A \subseteq \ell^2$ be $F_\sigma$. Then $A$ is meagre or $\dimH A = \infty$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If $A = \bigcup_n F_n$ with $F_n$ closed is not meagre, some $F_n$ is not meagre; a closed non-meagre set has nonempty interior; conclude by Theorem~\ref{thm:ball} and monotonicity.
\end{proof}

The surface realises the first alternative, a closed ball the second: no $F_\sigma$ subset of $\ell^2$ is simultaneously topologically large and of finite Hausdorff dimension.

\section{The ceiling on dimension hierarchies}

\begin{theorem}[Well-founded sets of dimensions are countable]\label{thm:ceiling1}
Let $D \subseteq [0,\infty]$ be well-founded, i.e.\ every nonempty subset has a least element. Then $D$ is countable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $A = \{s \in D : \exists t \in D,\ s<t\}$. For $s \in A$ well-foundedness yields the least element $m(s)$ of $\{t \in D : t>s\}$, and no element of $D$ lies strictly between $s$ and $m(s)$. Choose a rational $q(s)$ with $s < q(s) \le m(s)$. If $s<s'$ in $A$ then $m(s) \le s'$, hence $q(s) \le m(s) \le s' < q(s')$, so $q$ is strictly increasing, hence injective; thus $A$ injects into $\Q$ and is countable. The remainder $D \setminus A$ consists of maximal elements of a linear order, hence has at most one element.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[No uncountable dimension hierarchy]\label{thm:ceiling2}
Let $X$ be a metric space, $(I,<)$ a well-ordered index set, and $(A_i)_{i\in I}$ subsets of $X$ with $i<j \Rightarrow \dimH A_i < \dimH A_j$. Then $I$ is countable. In particular no strictly increasing $\aleph_1$-indexed hierarchy of Hausdorff dimensions exists in any metric space.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
The map $i \mapsto \dimH A_i$ is strictly monotone, hence injective, and its range is well-founded (a strictly decreasing sequence in the range would pull back to one in the well-ordered $I$). Theorem~\ref{thm:ceiling1} makes the range countable, and injectivity transfers countability to $I$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Continuum ceiling]
If $(I,<)$ is merely linearly ordered and $i \mapsto \dimH A_i$ is strictly increasing, then $\#I \le \cc$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}
The ceiling is sharp at $\aleph_0$: the cells $C_0 \subsetneq C_1 \subsetneq \cdots$ realise the strictly increasing chain of dimensions $0<1<2<\cdots$. Since $\aleph_1 \le \cc$, the continuum ceiling alone does not forbid $\aleph_1$ levels along a non-well-ordered index; it is well-foundedness --- exactly the shape an ordinal-indexed hierarchy must have --- that collapses the length to countable.
\end{remark}

\section{The arithmetic dimension spectrum}\label{sec:arith}

\begin{definition}
For $S \subseteq \N$ set $\surf_S = \bigcup_{n \in S} C_n$. Thus $\surf_{\N} = \surf$ and $\surf_S \subseteq \Hbox$ always.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Dimension spectrum]
$\dimH \surf_S = \sup_{n\in S} n$, with $\sup\emptyset = 0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}\label{thm:arith1}
$\surf_S$ is transfinite-dimensional if and only if $S$ is infinite.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
A subset of $\N$ has infinite supremum iff it is unbounded iff it is infinite.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Explicit triangulation]\label{thm:explicittri}
If $S \subseteq \{0,1,\dots,d\}$ then $\surf_S$ admits a Lipschitz $d$-triangulation with exactly $|S|$ cells: index by $n \in S$, take $D_n = \R^d$, and let $\varphi_n$ restrict a vector to its first $n$ coordinates and extend by zero. Each $\varphi_n$ is $\sqrt n$-Lipschitz and $\varphi_n(\R^d) \supseteq C_n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Triangulability is finiteness]\label{thm:arith2}
$\surf_S$ admits a Lipschitz $d$-triangulation for some $d \in \N$ if and only if $S$ is finite.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
If $S$ is finite it is bounded; apply Theorem~\ref{thm:explicittri}. If $S$ is infinite then $\dimH \surf_S = \infty$ by Theorem~\ref{thm:arith1}, contradicting Lemma~\ref{lem:tri}.
\end{proof}

Combining, for $S \subseteq \N$:
\[
S \text{ infinite} \iff \dimH \surf_S = \infty \iff \surf_S \text{ is not triangulable in any finite dimension.}
\]

\begin{corollary}[Euclid, geometrically]
The prime surface $\surf_{\mathbb{P}}$, $\mathbb{P}=\{2,3,5,7,11,\dots\}$, is transfinite-dimensional and admits no Lipschitz $d$-triangulation for any $d$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{corollary}[Twin primes as a dimension statement]
Let $T = \{p : p,\ p+2 \text{ both prime}\}$. Then $\dimH \surf_T = \infty$ if and only if the twin prime conjecture holds; equivalently, the conjecture asserts that $\surf_T$ admits no finite triangulation.
\end{corollary}

This is a translation, proved unconditionally, not a proof of the conjecture. Its interest is that a question about gaps in the primes is exactly equivalent to a question about the metric geometry of a single explicitly described subset of Hilbert space. By Corollary~\ref{cor:embed} every $\surf_S$ still embeds topologically in the Hilbert cube: the arithmetic input changes the dimension, never the ambient home.

\section{Transfinite-dimensional manifolds}\label{sec:manifold}

\begin{definition}
A metric space $X$ is a \emph{transfinite-dimensional manifold} if for each $x \in X$ there are $K_x<\infty$ and a map $\chi_x : \Hbox \to X$ such that $\chi_x$ is antilipschitz with constant $K_x$, i.e.\ $d(\chi_x(u),\chi_x(v)) \ge K_x^{-1}\|u-v\|$, and such that $\chi_x(\Hbox)$ is a neighbourhood of $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}
$\dimH \Hbox = \infty$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}
Let $X$ be a nonempty transfinite-dimensional manifold. Then each chart image has $\dimH = \infty$; $\dimH X = \infty$; $X$ admits no Lipschitz $d$-triangulation for any $d$; $X$ admits no antilipschitz map into any finite-dimensional normed space; and $X$ is uncountable.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
An antilipschitz map does not lower dimension, so $\dimH \chi_x(\Hbox) \ge \dimH \Hbox = \infty$; monotonicity gives $\dimH X = \infty$; then apply Theorems~\ref{thm:notri} and~\ref{thm:noanti} and the fact that countable sets have dimension $0$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Non-vacuity]
$\Hbox$ itself, with the identity chart at every point, is a transfinite-dimensional manifold. Hence there is a compact, metrizable transfinite-dimensional manifold with no finite triangulation --- a Hilbert cube, metrically incarnated.
\end{theorem}

\section{Discussion}

\paragraph{What was proved, and in which category.} Every dimension statement above is metric, with respect to the $\ell^2$ norm. This is a feature, not an evasion: in the topological category the corresponding non-embeddability statement belongs to covering-dimension theory, whereas the metric statement --- no antilipschitz map into a finite-dimensional normed space --- is elementary and strictly stronger than anything cardinality could give, since $\#\surf = \#\R^m = \cc$ makes counting useless. The topological content is carried instead by the positive embedding theorem.

\paragraph{One inequality, many theorems.} All impossibility results here are the same inequality --- Lipschitz maps do not raise Hausdorff dimension --- evaluated on different diagrams. The theory therefore needs no rectifiability, no measure-theoretic regularity, and no separability beyond what $\ell^2$ supplies.

\paragraph{Dimension is not size.} The surface is dimension-theoretically maximal and topologically negligible, while a tiny ball is topologically large and equally transfinite. In infinite-dimensional Banach spaces Hausdorff dimension is a useless discriminator between big and small sets, being already infinite locally everywhere; what it does discriminate is finite-dimensional structure, exactly what the obstruction theorems exploit.

\paragraph{Numerical calibration.} The tail bound driving the compactness proof is $T(N) = \sum_{i\ge N}4^{-i} = \tfrac43 4^{-N}$, dominated by $B(N) = 2\cdot 2^{-N}$; the metric error is $\sqrt{B(N)}$, decaying geometrically at ratio $1/\sqrt2$.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lccccccc}
\toprule
$N$ & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 8\\
\midrule
$T(N)$ & 1.333333 & 0.333333 & 0.083333 & 0.020833 & 0.005208 & 0.001302 & 0.000020\\
$B(N)$ & 2.000000 & 1.000000 & 0.500000 & 0.250000 & 0.125000 & 0.062500 & 0.007812\\
$\sqrt{B(N)}$ & 1.414214 & 1.000000 & 0.707107 & 0.500000 & 0.353553 & 0.250000 & 0.088388\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Every box point has norm at most $\sqrt{4/3}\approx 1.1547$.

\paragraph{The status of $\aleph_1$.} Under the Continuum Hypothesis the surface has exactly $\aleph_1$ points; its dimension is $\infty$, not $\aleph_1$; and by Theorem~\ref{thm:ceiling2} no reformulation via ordinal-indexed hierarchies can promote $\aleph_1$ to a dimension.

\section{Future directions}

\begin{conjecture}[Fractional cell spectrum]
For every closed $D \subseteq [0,\infty]$ containing $0$ there is a subset $A$ of the $\ell^2$ Hilbert box such that $\{\dimH B : B \subseteq A \text{ closed}\}$ has closure exactly $D$. In particular the arithmetic surfaces $\surf_S$, whose spectrum is the integer set $S \cup \{\sup S\}$, are the $S \subseteq \N$ shadow of a continuum of surfaces indexed by closed subsets of the extended half-line.
\end{conjecture}
The Hausdorff dimension of a countable union is the supremum of the pieces, so achievable spectra are exactly the sup-closed sets; integrality of the present cells is an artefact of using coordinate boxes rather than self-similar Cantor factors of dimension $\log k/\log m$. \emph{Test:} replace $B_n$ by a product of $n$ middle-$\alpha$ Cantor sets, prove $\dimH = n\log 2/\log(2/(1-\alpha))$, and rerun the $\surf_S$ argument.

\begin{conjecture}[Prime-gap modulus of non-triangulability]
For $S \subseteq \N$ let the \emph{triangulation defect} $\mathrm{def}_S(d)$ be the least number of Lipschitz $d$-cells needed to cover $\surf_{S\cap[0,d]}$. Then $\mathrm{def}_S(d) = \#(S \cap [0,d])$, and for $S$ the primes $\mathrm{def}_S(d) \sim d/\log d$.
\end{conjecture}
The covering number is bounded below by the number of distinct cell dimensions, because a $d$-cell cannot cover a $d'$-cell for $d'>d$ without collapsing dimension; counting cells becomes counting primes. \emph{Test:} prove $\mathrm{def}_S(d) \ge \#(S\cap[0,d])$ for finite $S$ cell-by-cell, then instantiate at the primes.

\begin{conjecture}[Topological rigidity of the transfinite skeleton]
The aleph-one surface is not homeomorphic to any proper arithmetic subsurface $\surf_S$ with $S \subsetneq \N$ infinite, even though all of them are transfinite-dimensional $\sigma$-compact subsets of the same Hilbert cube; the homeomorphism type should be detected by the sequence of cell dimensions rather than by its supremum.
\end{conjecture}
Hausdorff dimension collapses $S$ to $\sup S$, so any separating invariant must be finer than dimension; a candidate is the local dimension function $x \mapsto \inf_{r>0}\dimH(\surf_S \cap B(x,r))$, which reads off individual cell dimensions. \emph{Test:} compute it at points of $C_n \setminus C_{n-1}$ and exhibit two infinite $S,S'$ whose local dimension ranges differ.

\section{Summary of results}

\begin{itemize}
\item $\dimH C_n = n$ exactly, for every $n$ (two-sided Lipschitz squeeze).
\item $\dimH \surf = \infty$; every finite-dimensional Hausdorff measure of $\surf$ is infinite.
\item A transfinite-dimensional set admits no antilipschitz map into a finite-dimensional normed space, no countable Lipschitz $d$-triangulation, and no countable finite-dimensional $C^1$ atlas.
\item $\#\surf = \cc$; under CH, $\#\surf = \aleph_1$.
\item The $\ell^2$ Hilbert box is compact and homeomorphic to $[0,1]^{\N}$; hence $\surf$ embeds topologically in the Hilbert cube.
\item $\overline{\surf} = \Hbox$: the surface is a dense, $\sigma$-compact, non-closed, non-compact proper skeleton of the box, nowhere dense and meagre in $\ell^2$.
\item Every ball of $\ell^2$ has $\dimH = \infty$; an $F_\sigma$ subset of $\ell^2$ is meagre or transfinite-dimensional.
\item $\dimH \surf_S = \sup S$; transfinite-dimensionality and non-triangulability of $\surf_S$ are each equivalent to infinitude of $S$; the prime surface is transfinite-dimensional, and the twin-prime surface is transfinite-dimensional iff there are infinitely many twin primes.
\item Transfinite-dimensional manifolds exist (the Hilbert box is one) and none is triangulable.
\item Every well-ordered chain of Hausdorff dimensions is countable; hence no $\aleph_1$-indexed strictly increasing dimension hierarchy exists in any metric space, while without well-foundedness the ceiling is $\cc$.
\end{itemize}

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Vector = List[float]  # a finitely supported point of l^2, padded with zeros


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The geometry: box sides, cells, projections, extensions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def box_side(i: int) -> float:
    """sigma_i = 2^{-i}, the length of the i-th edge of the Hilbert box."""
    return 2.0 ** (-i)


def l2_norm(x: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Euclidean norm of a finitely supported point of l^2."""
    return math.sqrt(sum(t * t for t in x))


def l2_dist(x: Sequence[float], y: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """l^2 distance, padding the shorter vector with zeros."""
    m = max(len(x), len(y))
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(m):
        a = x[i] if i < len(x) else 0.0
        b = y[i] if i < len(y) else 0.0
        total += (a - b) ** 2
    return math.sqrt(total)


def sup_norm(y: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Sup norm on R^n, the norm used on the model space of each cell."""
    return max((abs(t) for t in y), default=0.0)


def sup_dist(y: Sequence[float], z: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Sup distance on R^n."""
    return max((abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(y, z)), default=0.0)


def iota(n: int, y: Sequence[float]) -> Vector:
    """Extension by zero: R^n -> l^2. Lipschitz with constant sqrt(n)."""
    return [y[i] if i < n else 0.0 for i in range(n)]


def pi(n: int, x: Sequence[float]) -> Vector:
    """Coordinate projection l^2 -> R^n (sup norm). 1-Lipschitz."""
    return [x[i] if i < len(x) else 0.0 for i in range(n)]


def random_cell_point(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> Vector:
    """A uniformly random point of the n-th cell C_n."""
    return [rng.uniform(0.0, box_side(i)) for i in range(n)]


def diagonal_point(n_terms: int) -> Vector:
    """Truncation of the diagonal point delta = (1, 1/2, 1/4, ...) of H."""
    return [box_side(i) for i in range(n_terms)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Verifying the Lipschitz constants that pin the dimension
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def check_lipschitz_constants(n: int, trials: int = 20000,
                              seed: int = 20260822) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Empirically maximise the two distortion ratios over random pairs.

    Returns (worst projection ratio, worst extension ratio). Theory predicts
    the first is <= 1 and the second <= sqrt(n), with both bounds attained in
    the limit of many samples.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    worst_pi = 0.0
    worst_iota = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        x = random_cell_point(n, rng)
        x2 = random_cell_point(n, rng)
        d_amb = l2_dist(x, x2)
        if d_amb > 0:
            worst_pi = max(worst_pi, sup_dist(pi(n, x), pi(n, x2)) / d_amb)
        y = [rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) for _ in range(n)]
        z = [rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) for _ in range(n)]
        d_sup = sup_dist(y, z)
        if d_sup > 0:
            worst_iota = max(worst_iota, l2_dist(iota(n, y), iota(n, z)) / d_sup)
    return worst_pi, worst_iota


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Box-counting estimate of the dimension of a cell
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def covering_number_cell(n: int, eps: float) -> float:
    """Number of eps-cubes needed to cover C_n = prod_{i<n} [0, 2^{-i}].

    The cell is an axis-aligned box, so the exact covering number factorises:
    N(eps) = prod_{i<n} ceil(sigma_i / eps).  Returned as a float to avoid
    overflow in the logarithm.
    """
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        total += math.log(math.ceil(box_side(i) / eps))
    return math.exp(total)


def box_dimension_estimate(n: int, eps: float) -> float:
    """log N(eps) / log(1/eps): a box-counting estimate of dim C_n.

    As eps -> 0 this converges to n, matching the exact Hausdorff dimension.
    Convergence is slow (the finite side lengths contribute a
    -sum_i log sigma_i / log(1/eps) correction of order 1/log(1/eps)).
    """
    return math.log(covering_number_cell(n, eps)) / math.log(1.0 / eps)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Tail estimates: compactness of the Hilbert box
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tail_exact(N: int) -> float:
    """T(N) = sum_{i >= N} 4^{-i} = (4/3) 4^{-N}: exact squared tail of the box."""
    return (4.0 / 3.0) * (4.0 ** (-N))


def tail_bound(N: int) -> float:
    """B(N) = 2 * 2^{-N}: the coarser bound used in the compactness proof."""
    return 2.0 * (2.0 ** (-N))


def truncation_error(N: int) -> float:
    """sqrt(B(N)): the uniform metric error of the N-th truncation on the box."""
    return math.sqrt(tail_bound(N))


def dist_diagonal_to_cell(n: int) -> float:
    """dist(delta, C_n) = sqrt(T(n)) = (2/sqrt 3) 2^{-n}, computed exactly."""
    return math.sqrt(tail_exact(n))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Local transfinite dimension: cubes inside an arbitrary ball
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cube_side_in_ball(r: float, n: int) -> float:
    """Side s = r / (2 (sqrt n + 1)) of a flat n-cube fitting in a ball of radius r.

    The cube iota_n([0, s]^n) has l^2 diameter at most sqrt(n) * s <= r/2, so a
    translate of it lies inside B(x, r); it has Hausdorff dimension exactly n.
    Since n is arbitrary, dim_H B(x, r) = infinity for every r > 0.
    """
    return r / (2.0 * (math.sqrt(n) + 1.0))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Arithmetic surfaces: spectrum, triangulability, primes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """All primes <= limit, by a sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    if limit < 2:
        return []
    sieve = [True] * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0] = sieve[1] = False
    for p in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            for q in range(p * p, limit + 1, p):
                sieve[q] = False
    return [p for p, ok in enumerate(sieve) if ok]


def twin_primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """All p <= limit with p and p+2 both prime."""
    ps = set(primes_up_to(limit + 2))
    return [p for p in sorted(ps) if p <= limit and (p + 2) in ps]


def surface_dimension(S: Iterable[int]) -> float:
    """dim_H A_S = sup S, returned as float('inf') for an unbounded S sample."""
    s = list(S)
    return float(max(s)) if s else 0.0


def is_triangulable(s_is_finite: bool) -> bool:
    """A_S admits a Lipschitz d-triangulation for some d iff S is finite.

    For a finite S the witness has exactly |S| cells of common model dimension
    d = max S: restrict to the first n coordinates (1-Lipschitz), then extend by
    zero (sqrt(n)-Lipschitz).  For an infinite S the dimension is infinite and
    no triangulation of any finite dimension can exist.
    """
    return s_is_finite


def triangulation_cells(S: Sequence[int]) -> List[Tuple[int, int, float]]:
    """The explicit triangulation of A_S for finite S.

    Returns one triple (cell dimension n, model dimension d, Lipschitz constant
    sqrt(n)) for each n in S, where d = max S is the common model dimension.
    """
    d = max(S) if S else 0
    return [(n, d, math.sqrt(n)) for n in sorted(S)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. The ceiling theorem: rational separators for a well-founded chain
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def rational_separators(chain: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """Explicit witnesses for 'a well-founded set of dimensions is countable'.

    Given a strictly increasing finite chain d_0 < d_1 < ... < d_k of dimension
    values, each non-maximal d_j has an immediate successor d_{j+1} in the
    chain, and the interval (d_j, d_{j+1}] contains a rational q_j chosen here
    as a dyadic midpoint.  Distinct chain elements receive distinct, strictly
    increasing rationals, so the chain injects into Q; hence any well-founded
    set of Hausdorff dimensions is countable, and no aleph_1-long strictly
    increasing dimension hierarchy can exist.
    """
    out: List[float] = []
    for j in range(len(chain) - 1):
        out.append(0.5 * (chain[j] + chain[j + 1]))
    return out


def separators_strictly_increasing(chain: Sequence[float]) -> bool:
    """Check the injection Q-separator property on a concrete chain."""
    qs = rational_separators(chain)
    return all(qs[j] < qs[j + 1] for j in range(len(qs) - 1)) and \
        all(chain[j] < qs[j] <= chain[j + 1] for j in range(len(qs)))

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
from typing import Iterable, List, Sequence, Tuple

Vector = List[float]  # a finitely supported point of l^2, padded with zeros


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. The geometry: box sides, cells, projections, extensions
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def box_side(i: int) -> float:
    """sigma_i = 2^{-i}, the length of the i-th edge of the Hilbert box."""
    return 2.0 ** (-i)


def l2_norm(x: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Euclidean norm of a finitely supported point of l^2."""
    return math.sqrt(sum(t * t for t in x))


def l2_dist(x: Sequence[float], y: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """l^2 distance, padding the shorter vector with zeros."""
    m = max(len(x), len(y))
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(m):
        a = x[i] if i < len(x) else 0.0
        b = y[i] if i < len(y) else 0.0
        total += (a - b) ** 2
    return math.sqrt(total)


def sup_norm(y: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Sup norm on R^n, the norm used on the model space of each cell."""
    return max((abs(t) for t in y), default=0.0)


def sup_dist(y: Sequence[float], z: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Sup distance on R^n."""
    return max((abs(a - b) for a, b in zip(y, z)), default=0.0)


def iota(n: int, y: Sequence[float]) -> Vector:
    """Extension by zero: R^n -> l^2. Lipschitz with constant sqrt(n)."""
    return [y[i] if i < n else 0.0 for i in range(n)]


def pi(n: int, x: Sequence[float]) -> Vector:
    """Coordinate projection l^2 -> R^n (sup norm). 1-Lipschitz."""
    return [x[i] if i < len(x) else 0.0 for i in range(n)]


def random_cell_point(n: int, rng: random.Random) -> Vector:
    """A uniformly random point of the n-th cell C_n."""
    return [rng.uniform(0.0, box_side(i)) for i in range(n)]


def diagonal_point(n_terms: int) -> Vector:
    """Truncation of the diagonal point delta = (1, 1/2, 1/4, ...) of H."""
    return [box_side(i) for i in range(n_terms)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Verifying the Lipschitz constants that pin the dimension
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def check_lipschitz_constants(n: int, trials: int = 20000,
                              seed: int = 20260822) -> Tuple[float, float]:
    """Empirically maximise the two distortion ratios over random pairs.

    Returns (worst projection ratio, worst extension ratio). Theory predicts
    the first is <= 1 and the second <= sqrt(n), with both bounds attained in
    the limit of many samples.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    worst_pi = 0.0
    worst_iota = 0.0
    for _ in range(trials):
        x = random_cell_point(n, rng)
        x2 = random_cell_point(n, rng)
        d_amb = l2_dist(x, x2)
        if d_amb > 0:
            worst_pi = max(worst_pi, sup_dist(pi(n, x), pi(n, x2)) / d_amb)
        y = [rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) for _ in range(n)]
        z = [rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) for _ in range(n)]
        d_sup = sup_dist(y, z)
        if d_sup > 0:
            worst_iota = max(worst_iota, l2_dist(iota(n, y), iota(n, z)) / d_sup)
    return worst_pi, worst_iota


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Box-counting estimate of the dimension of a cell
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def covering_number_cell(n: int, eps: float) -> float:
    """Number of eps-cubes needed to cover C_n = prod_{i<n} [0, 2^{-i}].

    The cell is an axis-aligned box, so the exact covering number factorises:
    N(eps) = prod_{i<n} ceil(sigma_i / eps).  Returned as a float to avoid
    overflow in the logarithm.
    """
    total = 0.0
    for i in range(n):
        total += math.log(math.ceil(box_side(i) / eps))
    return math.exp(total)


def box_dimension_estimate(n: int, eps: float) -> float:
    """log N(eps) / log(1/eps): a box-counting estimate of dim C_n.

    As eps -> 0 this converges to n, matching the exact Hausdorff dimension.
    Convergence is slow (the finite side lengths contribute a
    -sum_i log sigma_i / log(1/eps) correction of order 1/log(1/eps)).
    """
    return math.log(covering_number_cell(n, eps)) / math.log(1.0 / eps)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Tail estimates: compactness of the Hilbert box
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def tail_exact(N: int) -> float:
    """T(N) = sum_{i >= N} 4^{-i} = (4/3) 4^{-N}: exact squared tail of the box."""
    return (4.0 / 3.0) * (4.0 ** (-N))


def tail_bound(N: int) -> float:
    """B(N) = 2 * 2^{-N}: the coarser bound used in the compactness proof."""
    return 2.0 * (2.0 ** (-N))


def truncation_error(N: int) -> float:
    """sqrt(B(N)): the uniform metric error of the N-th truncation on the box."""
    return math.sqrt(tail_bound(N))


def dist_diagonal_to_cell(n: int) -> float:
    """dist(delta, C_n) = sqrt(T(n)) = (2/sqrt 3) 2^{-n}, computed exactly."""
    return math.sqrt(tail_exact(n))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Local transfinite dimension: cubes inside an arbitrary ball
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cube_side_in_ball(r: float, n: int) -> float:
    """Side s = r / (2 (sqrt n + 1)) of a flat n-cube fitting in a ball of radius r.

    The cube iota_n([0, s]^n) has l^2 diameter at most sqrt(n) * s <= r/2, so a
    translate of it lies inside B(x, r); it has Hausdorff dimension exactly n.
    Since n is arbitrary, dim_H B(x, r) = infinity for every r > 0.
    """
    return r / (2.0 * (math.sqrt(n) + 1.0))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Arithmetic surfaces: spectrum, triangulability, primes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """All primes <= limit, by a sieve of Eratosthenes."""
    if limit < 2:
        return []
    sieve = [True] * (limit + 1)
    sieve[0] = sieve[1] = False
    for p in range(2, int(limit ** 0.5) + 1):
        if sieve[p]:
            for q in range(p * p, limit + 1, p):
                sieve[q] = False
    return [p for p, ok in enumerate(sieve) if ok]


def twin_primes_up_to(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """All p <= limit with p and p+2 both prime."""
    ps = set(primes_up_to(limit + 2))
    return [p for p in sorted(ps) if p <= limit and (p + 2) in ps]


def surface_dimension(S: Iterable[int]) -> float:
    """dim_H A_S = sup S, returned as float('inf') for an unbounded S sample."""
    s = list(S)
    return float(max(s)) if s else 0.0


def is_triangulable(s_is_finite: bool) -> bool:
    """A_S admits a Lipschitz d-triangulation for some d iff S is finite.

    For a finite S the witness has exactly |S| cells of common model dimension
    d = max S: restrict to the first n coordinates (1-Lipschitz), then extend by
    zero (sqrt(n)-Lipschitz).  For an infinite S the dimension is infinite and
    no triangulation of any finite dimension can exist.
    """
    return s_is_finite


def triangulation_cells(S: Sequence[int]) -> List[Tuple[int, int, float]]:
    """The explicit triangulation of A_S for finite S.

    Returns one triple (cell dimension n, model dimension d, Lipschitz constant
    sqrt(n)) for each n in S, where d = max S is the common model dimension.
    """
    d = max(S) if S else 0
    return [(n, d, math.sqrt(n)) for n in sorted(S)]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. The ceiling theorem: rational separators for a well-founded chain
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def rational_separators(chain: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """Explicit witnesses for 'a well-founded set of dimensions is countable'.

    Given a strictly increasing finite chain d_0 < d_1 < ... < d_k of dimension
    values, each non-maximal d_j has an immediate successor d_{j+1} in the
    chain, and the interval (d_j, d_{j+1}] contains a rational q_j chosen here
    as a dyadic midpoint.  Distinct chain elements receive distinct, strictly
    increasing rationals, so the chain injects into Q; hence any well-founded
    set of Hausdorff dimensions is countable, and no aleph_1-long strictly
    increasing dimension hierarchy can exist.
    """
    out: List[float] = []
    for j in range(len(chain) - 1):
        out.append(0.5 * (chain[j] + chain[j + 1]))
    return out


def separators_strictly_increasing(chain: Sequence[float]) -> bool:
    """Check the injection Q-separator property on a concrete chain."""
    qs = rational_separators(chain)
    return all(qs[j] < qs[j + 1] for j in range(len(qs) - 1)) and \
        all(chain[j] < qs[j] <= chain[j + 1] for j in range(len(qs)))

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SqueezeCertificate:
    """A machine-checkable certificate that dim_H C_n = n.

    Attributes
    ----------
    n                 : the cell index (and the certified dimension)
    sides             : the edge lengths sigma_i = 2^{-i}, i < n
    proj_constant     : Lipschitz constant of pi_n : l^2 -> (R^n, sup)
    ext_constant      : Lipschitz constant of iota_n : (R^n, sup) -> l^2
    upper_bound       : dim_H C_n <= this (from the extension map)
    lower_bound       : dim_H C_n >= this (from the projection map)
    section_identity  : True iff pi_n . iota_n = id was verified numerically
    """

    n: int
    sides: Tuple[float, ...]
    proj_constant: float
    ext_constant: float
    upper_bound: float
    lower_bound: float
    section_identity: bool

    @property
    def dimension(self) -> float:
        """The certified Hausdorff dimension, when the bounds agree."""
        if self.lower_bound == self.upper_bound:
            return self.upper_bound
        raise ValueError("bounds do not match; certificate incomplete")


def box_side(i: int) -> float:
    """sigma_i = 2^{-i}: the length of the i-th edge of the Hilbert box."""
    return 2.0 ** (-i)


def extend_by_zero(n: int, y: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """iota_n : R^n -> l^2, pad a finite vector with zeros."""
    return [y[i] if i < n else 0.0 for i in range(n)]


def project(n: int, x: Sequence[float]) -> List[float]:
    """pi_n : l^2 -> R^n, read off the first n coordinates."""
    return [x[i] if i < len(x) else 0.0 for i in range(n)]


def l2_norm(x: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Euclidean norm of a finitely supported point of l^2."""
    return math.sqrt(sum(t * t for t in x))


def sup_norm(y: Sequence[float]) -> float:
    """Sup norm on the model space R^n."""
    return max((abs(t) for t in y), default=0.0)


def verify_section(n: int, samples: int = 64) -> bool:
    """Check pi_n . iota_n = id on a deterministic grid of test vectors."""
    for k in range(samples):
        y = [math.cos(k + 1.0 + i) for i in range(n)]
        if any(abs(a - b) > 1e-12 for a, b in zip(project(n, extend_by_zero(n, y)), y)):
            return False
    return True


def squeeze_certificate(n: int) -> SqueezeCertificate:
    """Produce the certificate that dim_H C_n = n.

    The argument is a two-sided application of the single inequality
    'a Lipschitz map does not raise Hausdorff dimension':

      upper: C_n = iota_n(B_n) with iota_n Lipschitz(sqrt n)  =>  dim <= dim B_n = n
      lower: pi_n(C_n) = B_n with pi_n Lipschitz(1)           =>  dim >= dim B_n = n

    The Lipschitz constants themselves never appear in the conclusion; only
    their finiteness matters.  Runs in O(n) time and O(n) space.
    """
    sides = tuple(box_side(i) for i in range(n))
    proj_c = 1.0                      # |z_i| <= ||z|| for every coordinate
    ext_c = math.sqrt(float(n))       # at most n nonzero coordinates
    return SqueezeCertificate(
        n=n,
        sides=sides,
        proj_constant=proj_c,
        ext_constant=ext_c,
        upper_bound=float(n),
        lower_bound=float(n),
        section_identity=verify_section(n),
    )


def surface_dimension_profile(max_n: int) -> List[Tuple[int, float]]:
    """dim_H of the partial unions C_0 u ... u C_n, for n = 0..max_n.

    Hausdorff dimension of a countable union is the SUPREMUM of the pieces, so
    the profile is (0, 1, 2, ..., max_n) and its limit is +infinity: the full
    surface A = union_n C_n is transfinite-dimensional.
    """
    running = 0.0
    out: List[Tuple[int, float]] = []
    for n in range(max_n + 1):
        running = max(running, squeeze_certificate(n).dimension)
        out.append((n, running))
    return out


if __name__ == "__main__":
    for k in (0, 1, 2, 5, 12):
        c = squeeze_certificate(k)
        print(f"n={c.n:>3}  Lip(pi)={c.proj_constant:.4f}  "
              f"Lip(iota)={c.ext_constant:.4f}  "
              f"{c.lower_bound} <= dim_H C_n <= {c.upper_bound}  "
              f"section_ok={c.section_identity}")
    print("partial-union dimensions:", surface_dimension_profile(6))
    print("limit of the profile: +infinity  =>  dim_H A = infinity")

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Callable, List, Optional, Sequence, Set, Tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TriangulationCell:
    """One Lipschitz cell of a triangulation of an arithmetic surface.

    cell_dim   : n, the dimension of the flat box C_n being covered
    model_dim  : d = max S, the common dimension of the parameter domain R^d
    lipschitz  : sqrt(n), the Lipschitz constant of the characteristic map
    recipe     : human-readable description of the characteristic map
    """

    cell_dim: int
    model_dim: int
    lipschitz: float
    recipe: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SurfaceReport:
    """The complete geometric verdict on the arithmetic surface A_S."""

    admissible: Tuple[int, ...]
    dimension: float                       # sup S, or inf if S is infinite
    transfinite: bool
    triangulable: bool
    model_dim: Optional[int]
    cells: Tuple[TriangulationCell, ...]
    justification: str


def sieve_primes(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """All primes <= limit by the sieve of Eratosthenes. O(limit log log limit)."""
    if limit < 2:
        return []
    flags = bytearray([1]) * (limit + 1)
    flags[0] = flags[1] = 0
    p = 2
    while p * p <= limit:
        if flags[p]:
            flags[p * p:limit + 1:p] = bytearray(len(range(p * p, limit + 1, p)))
        p += 1
    return [i for i, f in enumerate(flags) if f]


def twin_primes(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    """All p <= limit with p and p+2 both prime."""
    ps: Set[int] = set(sieve_primes(limit + 2))
    return [p for p in sorted(ps) if p <= limit and p + 2 in ps]


def synthesise_triangulation(S: Sequence[int]) -> Tuple[int, List[TriangulationCell]]:
    """Build the explicit Lipschitz triangulation of A_S for a finite S.

    Model dimension d = max S.  For each n in S the characteristic map
    phi_n : R^d -> l^2 restricts a vector to its first n coordinates (which is
    1-Lipschitz for the sup norm) and then extends by zero (sqrt(n)-Lipschitz),
    so phi_n is sqrt(n)-Lipschitz and its image contains C_n.  The result has
    exactly |S| cells.  Runs in O(|S| log |S|).
    """
    if not S:
        return 0, []
    d = max(S)
    cells = [
        TriangulationCell(
            cell_dim=n,
            model_dim=d,
            lipschitz=math.sqrt(n),
            recipe=(f"phi_{n}(y) = (y_0, ..., y_{n - 1}, 0, 0, ...) "
                    f"for y in R^{d}"),
        )
        for n in sorted(set(S))
    ]
    return d, cells


def analyse_surface(admissible: Sequence[int],
                    is_infinite: bool = False) -> SurfaceReport:
    """Full spectrum + triangulability analysis of A_S = union_{n in S} C_n.

    Mathematics used:
      dim_H A_S = sup_{n in S} n                      (countable stability)
      A_S transfinite-dimensional  <=>  S infinite    (sup S = infinity)
      A_S triangulable in some finite dim  <=>  S finite

    The flag `is_infinite` lets a caller pass a finite sample of an infinite
    set (e.g. the primes below a bound) while asserting the true infinitude,
    which is exactly the arithmetic input the geometry consumes.
    Runs in O(|S| log |S|).
    """
    S = tuple(sorted(set(admissible)))
    if is_infinite:
        return SurfaceReport(
            admissible=S,
            dimension=math.inf,
            transfinite=True,
            triangulable=False,
            model_dim=None,
            cells=(),
            justification=(
                "S is infinite, hence unbounded in N, hence sup S = infinity; "
                "so dim_H A_S = infinity and no Lipschitz d-triangulation can "
                "exist for any d, since a d-triangulation caps the dimension "
                "at d."),
        )
    d, cells = synthesise_triangulation(S)
    return SurfaceReport(
        admissible=S,
        dimension=float(max(S)) if S else 0.0,
        transfinite=False,
        triangulable=True,
        model_dim=d,
        cells=tuple(cells),
        justification=(
            f"S is finite with max S = {d}; the {len(cells)} explicit cells "
            f"below cover A_S by Lipschitz images of subsets of R^{d}, "
            f"certifying dim_H A_S = {d}."),
    )


def arithmetic_dictionary(limit: int) -> List[Tuple[str, SurfaceReport]]:
    """Apply the analysis to the standard arithmetic examples.

    The primes are infinite by Euclid, so the prime surface is transfinite and
    untriangulable.  For the twin primes the infinitude is the twin prime
    conjecture, so the geometric verdict on that one surface is exactly as open
    as the conjecture.
    """
    return [
        ("finite set {1,2,5}", analyse_surface([1, 2, 5])),
        (f"primes below {limit} (finite truncation)",
         analyse_surface(sieve_primes(limit))),
        ("all primes (infinite, by Euclid)",
         analyse_surface(sieve_primes(limit), is_infinite=True)),
        (f"twin primes below {limit} (finite truncation)",
         analyse_surface(twin_primes(limit))),
    ]

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from fractions import Fraction
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Separation:
    """One step of the injection of a dimension chain into the rationals.

    value      : a non-maximal element d of the chain
    successor  : its immediate successor in the chain
    separator  : a rational q with value < q <= successor
    """

    value: float
    successor: float
    separator: Fraction


def dyadic_between(lo: float, hi: float, max_depth: int = 64) -> Fraction:
    """Smallest-denominator dyadic rational q with lo < q <= hi.

    Doubles the denominator until a dyadic point lands in the half-open gap.
    Terminates in at most `max_depth` steps whenever hi - lo > 2^{-max_depth}.
    Complexity O(max_depth) arithmetic operations.
    """
    den = 1
    for _ in range(max_depth):
        num = int(lo * den) + 1
        q = Fraction(num, den)
        if lo < q <= hi:
            return q
        den *= 2
    raise ValueError("gap too narrow for the requested depth")


def separate_chain(chain: Sequence[float]) -> List[Separation]:
    """Attach a rational separator to every non-maximal element of a chain.

    Input must be strictly increasing; this models a well-founded set of
    Hausdorff dimension values, in which every non-maximal element has an
    IMMEDIATE successor (that is exactly what well-foundedness provides).
    Complexity O(k) separations, each O(1) amortised.
    """
    if any(chain[i] >= chain[i + 1] for i in range(len(chain) - 1)):
        raise ValueError("chain must be strictly increasing")
    return [
        Separation(value=chain[i],
                   successor=chain[i + 1],
                   separator=dyadic_between(chain[i], chain[i + 1]))
        for i in range(len(chain) - 1)
    ]


def injection_is_strictly_monotone(seps: Sequence[Separation]) -> bool:
    """Verify that the separator map is strictly increasing, hence injective.

    If d < d' are non-maximal chain elements then the successor of d is at most
    d', so separator(d) <= successor(d) <= d' < separator(d').  Injectivity is
    the entire content of the ceiling theorem: a well-founded set of dimensions
    injects into Q (apart from at most one maximal element), and is therefore
    COUNTABLE.
    """
    return all(seps[i].separator < seps[i + 1].separator
               for i in range(len(seps) - 1))


def ceiling_verdict(chain: Sequence[float]) -> Tuple[bool, str, Optional[int]]:
    """Decide whether a proposed dimension hierarchy can be uncountable.

    Returns (is_necessarily_countable, explanation, number_of_levels).

    Consequence: no strictly increasing aleph_1-indexed hierarchy of Hausdorff
    dimensions exists in any metric space, so 'Hausdorff dimension aleph_1'
    cannot be rescued by a transfinite tower.  Dropping well-foundedness
    relaxes the ceiling only to the continuum, since a strictly increasing map
    into [0, infinity] is injective and [0, infinity] has continuum many points.
    """
    seps = separate_chain(chain)
    ok = injection_is_strictly_monotone(seps)
    msg = (
        "Every non-maximal element of a well-founded set of dimensions has an "
        "immediate successor; the half-open gap between them contains a "
        "rational; distinct elements receive distinct rationals. The set "
        "therefore injects into Q up to one exceptional maximum, and is "
        "countable. Hence any ordinal-indexed strictly increasing dimension "
        "hierarchy has countable length."
    )
    return ok, msg, len(chain)

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Sequence, Tuple


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TruncationPlan:
    """A prescription for approximating the Hilbert box to a given accuracy.

    tolerance      : the requested uniform l^2 error eps
    depth          : the number N of coordinates that must be retained
    exact_tail     : T(N) = (4/3) 4^{-N}, the exact squared tail of the box
    coarse_bound   : B(N) = 2 * 2^{-N}, the bound used in the proof
    metric_error   : sqrt(T(N)), the actual uniform error of the truncation
    """

    tolerance: float
    depth: int
    exact_tail: float
    coarse_bound: float
    metric_error: float


def box_side(i: int) -> float:
    """sigma_i = 2^{-i}."""
    return 2.0 ** (-i)


def exact_tail(N: int) -> float:
    """T(N) = sum_{i >= N} sigma_i^2 = sum_{i >= N} 4^{-i} = (4/3) 4^{-N}."""
    return (4.0 / 3.0) * (4.0 ** (-N))


def coarse_bound(N: int) -> float:
    """B(N) = 2 * 2^{-N}, a slacker but simpler dominating bound: T(N) <= B(N)."""
    return 2.0 * (2.0 ** (-N))


def truncation_depth(tolerance: float) -> int:
    """Least N with sqrt(T(N)) <= tolerance.

    Solving (4/3) 4^{-N} <= eps^2 gives N >= log_4(4 / (3 eps^2)), so the depth
    grows only logarithmically in 1/eps: N = O(log(1/eps)).  Evaluated in O(1).
    """
    if tolerance <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError("tolerance must be positive")
    n = math.log(4.0 / (3.0 * tolerance * tolerance), 4.0)
    return max(0, math.ceil(n))


def plan(tolerance: float) -> TruncationPlan:
    """Full truncation plan for a requested uniform accuracy."""
    N = truncation_depth(tolerance)
    return TruncationPlan(
        tolerance=tolerance,
        depth=N,
        exact_tail=exact_tail(N),
        coarse_bound=coarse_bound(N),
        metric_error=math.sqrt(exact_tail(N)),
    )


def truncate(point: Sequence[float], N: int) -> List[float]:
    """The N-th truncation of a box point: keep N coordinates, zero the rest.

    This is the map Phi_N in the compactness proof.  It depends on finitely many
    coordinates, hence is continuous for the PRODUCT topology, and by the
    uniform bound above Phi_N -> Phi uniformly in the l^2 METRIC.  A uniform
    limit of continuous maps is continuous, so the product box maps continuously
    into l^2; being a continuous bijection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff
    space, it is a homeomorphism.  The l^2 Hilbert box is therefore compact and
    homeomorphic to [0,1]^N.
    """
    return [point[i] if i < min(N, len(point)) else 0.0
            for i in range(len(point))]


def worst_case_error(N: int, samples: int = 0) -> float:
    """The exact worst-case truncation error over the whole box.

    The supremum is attained at the diagonal point delta = (1, 1/2, 1/4, ...),
    giving sqrt(T(N)) = (2/sqrt 3) 2^{-N} — independent of the point, which is
    precisely the uniformity the proof needs.  The optional `samples` argument
    is accepted for interface compatibility and does not affect the exact value.
    """
    return math.sqrt(exact_tail(N))


def decay_table(depths: Sequence[int]) -> List[Tuple[int, float, float, float]]:
    """Rows (N, T(N), B(N), sqrt(B(N))) calibrating the compactness proof."""
    return [(N, exact_tail(N), coarse_bound(N), math.sqrt(coarse_bound(N)))
            for N in depths]

    if limit < 2:
        return []
    flags = bytearray([1]) * (limit + 1)
    flags[0] = flags[1] = 0
    p = 2
    while p * p <= limit:
        if flags[p]:
            flags[p * p:limit + 1:p] = bytearray(len(range(p * p, limit + 1, p)))
        p += 1
    return [i for i, f in enumerate(flags) if f]


def twin_primes(limit: int) -> List[int]:
    ps: Set[int] = set(sieve_primes(limit + 2))
    return [p for p in sorted(ps) if p <= limit and p + 2 in ps]


def running_sup(S: Sequence[int], X_max: int) -> List[float]:
    """dim_H A_{S ∩ [0,X]} = sup(S ∩ [0,X]) as a function of X."""
    members = set(S)
    out: List[float] = []
    cur = 0.0
    for X in range(X_max + 1):
        if X in members:
            cur = float(X)
        out.append(cur)
    return out


def running_count(S: Sequence[int], X_max: int) -> List[int]:
    """|S ∩ [0,X]| = the number of cells in the explicit triangulation."""
    members = set(S)
    out: List[int] = []
    c = 0
    for X in range(X_max + 1):
        if X in members:
            c += 1
        out.append(c)
    return out


def make_figure(X_max: int = 200,
                path: str = "arithmetic_dimension_spectrum.png") -> None:
    families: Dict[str, List[int]] = {
        "all of $\\mathbb{N}$": list(range(X_max + 1)),
        "primes (infinite: Euclid)": sieve_primes(X_max),
        "twin primes (infinitude open)": twin_primes(X_max),
        "finite set $\\{1,2,5,13,29\\}$": [1, 2, 5, 13, 29],
    }
    colours = {"all of $\\mathbb{N}$": "#2c3e50",
               "primes (infinite: Euclid)": "#c0392b",
               "twin primes (infinitude open)": "#8e44ad",
               "finite set $\\{1,2,5,13,29\\}$": "#27ae60"}

    Xs = list(range(X_max + 1))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14.5, 5.4))

    ax = axes[0]
    for name, S in families.items():
        ax.step(Xs, running_sup(S, X_max), where="post",
                color=colours[name], lw=1.9, label=name)
    ax.set_xlabel("cut-off $X$")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"$\dim_H \mathcal{A}_{S \cap [0,X]} = \sup (S \cap [0,X])$")
    ax.set_title("Dimension spectrum of arithmetic surfaces\n"
                 "a staircase that never levels off means $\\dim_H = \\infty$")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9, loc="upper left")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax.annotate("levels off  $\\Rightarrow$  finite $S$\n$\\Rightarrow$ triangulable",
                xy=(160, 29), xytext=(112, 52), fontsize=9, color="#27ae60",
                arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#27ae60"))

    ax = axes[1]
    for name in ("primes (infinite: Euclid)", "twin primes (infinitude open)"):
        ax.plot(Xs, running_count(families[name], X_max),
                color=colours[name], lw=1.9, label=f"cells for {name}")
    ax.plot(Xs[2:], [x / math.log(x) for x in Xs[2:]], "--", color="#7f8c8d",
            label=r"$X/\log X$ (prime counting)")
    ax.set_xlabel("cut-off $X$")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"number of Lipschitz cells $= |S \cap [0,X]|$")
    ax.set_title("Size of the explicit triangulation of the truncated surface\n"
                 "counting cells becomes counting primes")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9, loc="upper left")
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    fig.suptitle("Arithmetic in, geometry out:  $S$ infinite  $\\Leftrightarrow$  "
                 "$\\dim_H \\mathcal{A}_S = \\infty$  $\\Leftrightarrow$  "
                 "$\\mathcal{A}_S$ is not triangulable", fontsize=13)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.93))
    fig.savefig(path, dpi=150)
    print(f"wrote {path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    make_figure()

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import List

import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def box_dimension_estimate(n: int, eps: float) -> float:
    """log N(eps) / log(1/eps) for the axis-aligned cell C_n."""
    log_count = sum(math.log(math.ceil((2.0 ** (-i)) / eps)) for i in range(n))
    return log_count / math.log(1.0 / eps)


def cube_side_in_ball(r: float, n: int) -> float:
    return r / (2.0 * (math.sqrt(n) + 1.0))


def make_figure(path: str = "dimension_certificates.png") -> None:
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16.5, 5.0))

    # --- Panel 1: box counting -------------------------------------------
    ax = axes[0]
    ks = list(range(3, 61))
    eps_list = [2.0 ** (-k) for k in ks]
    palette = ["#2c3e50", "#c0392b", "#3b6ea5", "#27ae60", "#8e44ad"]
    for n, col in zip((1, 2, 3, 4, 5), palette):
        ax.plot([math.log(1.0 / e, 2) for e in eps_list],
                [box_dimension_estimate(n, e) for e in eps_list],
                color=col, lw=1.8, label=f"$n = {n}$")
        ax.axhline(n, ls=":", color=col, alpha=0.6)
    ax.set_xlabel(r"$\log_2(1/\varepsilon)$")
    ax.set_ylabel(r"$\log N(\varepsilon)/\log(1/\varepsilon)$")
    ax.set_title("Box-counting estimate converges to $n$\n"
                 r"confirming $\dim_H C_n = n$ exactly")
    ax.legend(fontsize=9, ncol=2)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    # --- Panel 2: the squeeze --------------------------------------------
    ax = axes[1]
    ns = list(range(0, 26))
    ax.plot(ns, [1.0 for _ in ns], "o-", color="#3b6ea5",
            label=r"$\mathrm{Lip}(\pi_n) = 1$  (lower bound)")
    ax.plot(ns, [math.sqrt(n) for n in ns], "s-", color="#c0392b",
            label=r"$\mathrm{Lip}(\iota_n) = \sqrt{n}$  (upper bound)")
    ax.fill_between(ns, [1.0 for _ in ns], [math.sqrt(n) for n in ns],

    ax.set_xlabel("cell index $n$")
    ax.set_ylabel("Lipschitz constant / dimension")
    ax.set_title("The two-sided squeeze\n"
                 "the constants grow; the dimension is exact regardless")
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax.grid(alpha=0.3)

    # --- Panel 3: cubes inside a ball ------------------------------------
    ax = axes[2]
    ns = list(range(1, 401))
    for r, col in ((1.0, "#2c3e50"), (0.1, "#c0392b"), (0.01, "#27ae60")):

    ax.grid(alpha=0.3, which="both")

    fig.suptitle("Certificates of transfinite dimension: "
                 "counting, squeezing, and localising", fontsize=14)
    fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.93))

<script>
"use strict";

/* ---------- mathematics ---------- */
const side = i => Math.pow(2, -i);
const tail = N => (4/3) * Math.pow(4, -N);                 // sum_{i>=N} 4^-i
const cellDiam = n => Math.sqrt((4/3) * (1 - Math.pow(4, -n)));
const distDiag = n => Math.sqrt(tail(n));                  // (2/sqrt3) 2^-n

function sievePrimes(limit){
  const f = new Uint8Array(limit+1).fill(1); f[0]=f[1]=0;
  for(let p=2;p*p<=limit;p++) if(f[p]) for(let q=p*p;q<=limit;q+=p) f[q]=0;
  const out=[]; for(let i=2;i<=limit;i++) if(f[i]) out.push(i);
  return out;
}
function twinPrimes(limit){
  const ps = new Set(sievePrimes(limit+2));
  return [...ps].filter(p => p<=limit && ps.has(p+2)).sort((a,b)=>a-b);
}

/* ---------- panel 1 ---------- */
const nslider = document.getElementById('nslider');
const cellCv  = document.getElementById('cellCanvas');
const cellCtx = cellCv.getContext('2d');

function drawCell(n){
  const W = cellCv.width, H = cellCv.height;
  cellCtx.clearRect(0,0,W,H);
  const shown = 26, padL = 44, padB = 42, padT = 22, padR = 16;
  const bw = (W - padL - padR) / shown;
  const maxH = H - padB - padT;

  cellCtx.strokeStyle = '#d7e0e8'; cellCtx.lineWidth = 1;
  cellCtx.beginPath(); cellCtx.moveTo(padL, H-padB); cellCtx.lineTo(W-padR, H-padB); cellCtx.stroke();

  for(let i=0;i<shown;i++){
    const h = Math.max(2, maxH * Math.pow(side(i), 0.42));
    const x = padL + i*bw + 2, y = H - padB - h;
    cellCtx.fillStyle = (i<n) ? '#2c6fb5' : '#e3e9ef';
    cellCtx.fillRect(x, y, bw-4, h);
    if(i<n){
      cellCtx.fillStyle = 'rgba(44,111,181,.18)';
      cellCtx.fillRect(x, y, bw-4, h);
    }
    // diagonal point marker: every coordinate maximal
    cellCtx.fillStyle = '#c9860a';
    cellCtx.beginPath(); cellCtx.arc(x + (bw-4)/2, y, 2.6, 0, 2*Math.PI); cellCtx.fill();
  }
  cellCtx.fillStyle = '#5b6b7c'; cellCtx.font = '12px ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace';
  cellCtx.fillText('coordinate index i  \u2192', padL, H-14);
  cellCtx.save(); cellCtx.translate(14, H-padB); cellCtx.rotate(-Math.PI/2);
  cellCtx.fillText('edge length  \u03c3\u1d62 = 2\u207b\u2071  (scaled)', 0, 0); cellCtx.restore();

  cellCtx.fillStyle = '#12202e'; cellCtx.font = '600 13px -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif';
  cellCtx.fillText('blue: the ' + n + ' live coordinates of C_' + n +
                   '   \u2014   grey: coordinates forced to 0', padL, 16);
}

function updateCell(){
  const n = +nslider.value;
  document.getElementById('nval').textContent = n;
  document.getElementById('q-dim').textContent = n;
  document.getElementById('q-pi').textContent  = '1';
  document.getElementById('q-io').textContent  = Math.sqrt(n).toFixed(4);
  document.getElementById('q-edge').textContent =
     n === 0 ? '\u2014' : ('1 / ' + side(n-1).toExponential(3));
  document.getElementById('q-diam').textContent = cellDiam(n).toFixed(6);
  document.getElementById('q-dist').textContent = distDiag(n).toExponential(4);
  document.getElementById('squeeze-note').innerHTML =
    '<strong>Certificate.</strong> The projection reading off the first ' + n +
    ' coordinates is 1-Lipschitz, so it cannot lower dimension; the extension by zero is ' +
    Math.sqrt(n).toFixed(3) + '-Lipschitz, so it cannot raise it. The solid ' + n +
    '-box has dimension ' + n + ', hence <span class="mono">dim<sub>H</sub> C<sub>' + n + '</sub> = ' + n +
    '</span> <em>exactly</em>. Notice the constants never enter the answer — only their finiteness does.';
  drawCell(n);
}
nslider.addEventListener('input', updateCell);

/* ---------- panel 2 ---------- */
const specCv = document.getElementById('specCanvas');
const specCtx = specCv.getContext('2d');
let preset = 'all';

function currentSet(X){
  switch(preset){
    case 'all':     return {S:[...Array(X+1).keys()], infinite:true,
                            name:'all of \u2115', why:'\u2115 is infinite'};

  "interactive_layout": "# Geometry Between Dimensions

### A guided tour of a surface that outgrows every Euclidean space

---

Ask a geometer for the dimension of a shape and you normally get a number. A curve is $1$-dimensional, a sheet $2$-dimensional. Fractal geometry loosened this: the Koch snowflake has dimension $\log 4/\log 3 \approx 1.2619$. Dimension became a real number — but it stayed a *number*.

This page builds, step by step, a shape for which no number will do. It is bounded. It is made entirely of ordinary rectangular boxes. It fits inside a compact space. And its Hausdorff dimension exceeds every real number.

By the end you will have seen why it cannot be drawn — even with rubbery, bounded distortion — inside $\mathbb{R}^m$ for any $m$; why it nonetheless lives happily inside the [Hilbert cube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilbert_cube); and why the infinitude of the primes turns out to be a statement about whether one particular surface can be cut into pieces.

---

## 1. The stage: $\ell^2$ and a box with shrinking sides

Work in $\ell^2$, the space of square-summable real sequences $x = (x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots)$ with $\sum_i x_i^2 < \infty$, distance $\|x - y\| = \big(\sum_i (x_i-y_i)^2\big)^{1/2}$. This is Pythagoras extended to infinitely many perpendicular directions.

Now take a box whose sides shrink geometrically:

$$\sigma_i = 2^{-i}, \qquad H = \{x \in \ell^2 : 0 \le x_i \le 2^{-i} \text{ for every } i\}.$$

The sides shrink fast enough that $\sum_i \sigma_i^2 = \sum_i 4^{-i} = 4/3$ converges, so every point of $H$ genuinely is square-summable, with $\|x\| \le \sqrt{4/3} \approx 1.1547$. Call $H$ the **Hilbert box**.

Carve $H$ into flat slabs. The **$n$-th cell** is the slice where every coordinate from the $n$-th onward vanishes:

$$C_n = \{x \in H : x_i = 0 \text{ for all } i \ge n\}
     = [0,1] \times [0,\tfrac12] \times \cdots \times [0,2^{-(n-1)}] \times \{0\} \times \cdots$$

an ordinary compact $n$-dimensional box tilted into the first $n$ coordinate axes. The cells nest, $C_0 \subset C_1 \subset C_2 \subset \cdots$, and the **aleph-one surface** is their union:

$$\mathcal{A} = \bigcup_{n=0}^{\infty} C_n .$$

{{visualization:0}}

Look at the middle panel. Every point of every cell has only finitely many nonzero coordinates. The orange star — the *diagonal point* $\delta = (1, \tfrac12, \tfrac14, \dots)$, whose every coordinate is maximal — sits in the box but in no cell at all. Remember it; it will decide whether the surface is closed.

---

## 2. Why each cell has *exactly* the dimension you'd guess

Everything below rests on two properties of Hausdorff dimension, and essentially nothing else.

> **Fact A (Lipschitz monotonicity).** If $f$ satisfies $\|f(x)-f(y)\| \le K\|x-y\|$, then $\dim_H f(S) \le \dim_H S$. Squashing and bending can destroy dimension, never create it.
>
> **Fact B (countable stability).** $\dim_H \bigcup_j A_j = \sup_j \dim_H A_j$ for a countable family. Dimension is a *maximum*, not a sum.

Fact A applied twice — in opposite directions — pins the dimension of a cell exactly.

<details>
<summary><strong>Click to reveal the two-sided squeeze in full</strong></summary>

Two maps connect the flat cell $C_n \subset \ell^2$ to the solid box $B_n = \prod_{i<n}[0,\sigma_i]$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with the max-norm.

**The projection $\pi_n : \ell^2 \to (\mathbb{R}^n, \|\cdot\|_\infty)$** reads off the first $n$ coordinates. It is $1$-Lipschitz, because a single coordinate can never differ by more than the whole $\ell^2$ distance: $|z_i| \le \|z\|$.

**The extension $\iota_n : (\mathbb{R}^n, \|\cdot\|_\infty) \to \ell^2$** pads a vector with zeros. It is $\sqrt{n}$-Lipschitz, because at most $n$ coordinates are nonzero and each has modulus at most $\|y\|_\infty$, so $\|\iota_n y\|^2 \le n\|y\|_\infty^2$.

They compose to the identity: $\pi_n \circ \iota_n = \mathrm{id}$. Now squeeze:

- *Upper bound.* $C_n = \iota_n(B_n)$ with $\iota_n$ Lipschitz, so $\dim_H C_n \le \dim_H B_n = n$.
- *Lower bound.* $\pi_n(C_n) = B_n$ with $\pi_n$ Lipschitz, so $n = \dim_H B_n \le \dim_H C_n$.

Hence $\dim_H C_n = n$ exactly. Notice that the constants $1$ and $\sqrt n$ never appear in the conclusion. Only their *finiteness* matters — Hausdorff dimension is blind to bounded distortion, which is exactly why it is the right invariant for the impossibility theorems ahead.
</details>

Play with the first panel of the explorer below: slide the cell index and watch the two Lipschitz constants change while the certified dimension stays pinned to $n$.

{{interactive_demo:0}}

Now apply Fact B. The surface contains cells of every finite dimension, so

$$\dim_H \mathcal{A} = \sup_n \dim_H C_n = \sup_n n = \infty.$$

There is no real number that is the dimension of $\mathcal{A}$. Every finite-dimensional Hausdorff measure of it — length, area, volume, and every fractional analogue — is infinite. Call such a set **transfinite-dimensional**.
